subject: Density functions on the normal scale

messages.author: e751b45c437d9866
messages.subject: Density functions on the normal scale
parts:
Hi all! 

Is there a way to obtain the density function of a r.v. on the normal scale without exponentiating the result of the log scale? 
I mean a statement like 

pag[t] <- poisson(N[t], lambda[t]); 

instead of

diag_pag[t] <- poisson_log(N[t], lambda[t]); 
pag[t] <- exp(diag_pag[t]); 

I noticed that the exp function has a really negative impact on the performance of my code. 

Giorgio

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Density functions on the normal scale
parts:
Any hint as to why you need it on the linear scale? You usually
want to keep everything on the log scale at all times because the
linear scale is so unstable for probability densities.

So no, there's no direct density functions built into the Stan
language. You can implement poisson directly, but you'll find
it has

poisson(y, lambda) = pow(lambda,y) * exp(-lambda) / gamma(y + 1)

But you very quickly run into overflow and underflow issues on
the linear scale if you do this directly rather than exponentiating
on the log scale (e.g., lambda better be < 750 or so or exp(-lambda)
will underflow to zero).

- Bob
